tb25-actions-001:actions-01.rationale: DBP establishes both ketawa and tertawa for laughter, but this dictionary result does not establish an everyday national preference.

sources.observation: DBP glosses ketawa with tertawa, confirming overlap without frequency.

tb25-actions-001:actions-02.rationale: A current Malaysian education headline naturally uses membincangkan for discussion; the named alternative remains unquantified.

sources.observation: Higher education ministry headline uses membincangkan topik.

tb25-actions-001:actions-03.rationale: Malaysian legal text uses menangguhkan and menunda for the same postponement action; relative everyday preference is not established.

sources.observation: The legal provision explicitly pairs menangguhkan and menunda.

tb25-actions-001:actions-04.rationale: A Malaysian family article uses both melintas and menyeberang for crossing a road; the proposed preference distinction may be weaker than stated.

sources.observation: The same road-safety article uses both forms.

tb25-actions-001:actions-05.rationale: A Malaysian government answer uses both mengembalikan barang and memulangkan barang in the same return-of-goods scenario.

sources.observation: Question and answer use the competing phrases for returning goods.

tb25-food-001:food-01.rationale: A current Malaysian food menu uses pencuci mulut for dessert, including alongside English dessert product wording.

sources.observation: Domino’s Malaysian menu offers a pencuci mulut section and dessert promotion.

tb25-health-001:health-05.rationale: Malaysian marketplace products use pembalut luka alongside English bandage; source supports commercial use but does not settle whether this is the best generic everyday answer.

sources.observation: Marketplace product listings include both terms and multiple dressing types.

tb25-home-001:home-03.rationale: Malaysian retail listings use both baju tidur and pyjama, so the national preference distinction remains uncertain.

sources.observation: Marketplace listings present baju tidur and pyjama terms together.

tb25-technology-001:technology-01.rationale: A Malaysian government technical page uses pangkalan data in prose while English database appears in the project name; localized term is usable in technical communication, but everyday preference is unproven.

sources.observation: Sabah government page uses pangkalan data for the Registered Entity Database in Malay body text.

tb25-technology-001:technology-03.rationale: Indonesian Microsoft product language supports lembar bentang but also uses spreadsheet; Malaysian hamparan elektronik was not confirmed by an ordinary-use source in this bounded lookup.

sources.observation: Microsoft Excel Indonesian page uses lembar bentang in the title and spreadsheet in product wording.

tb25-technology-001:technology-04.rationale: Malaysia’s live transport dashboard uses pengangkutan awam for the bus and rail category; this supports normal institutional use, though no frequency comparison was made.

sources.observation: Current Malaysian national transport dashboard labels the category Pengangkutan Awam.

tb25-technology-001:technology-05.rationale: Malaysian government program uses latihan kerja in an employment-training context; shared wording and exact preferred phrase require further audit.

sources.observation: Agriculture employment program uses latihan kerja for on-the-job training.

research_operations.notes: Batched public-source searches and page inspection; source records are claim-limited and are not frequency estimates.
